sop_requirements.value: A letter of intent is part of the application and is considered in the admissions evaluation together with GPA and references.
sop_requirements.evidence_snippet: Both your final-year GPA and overall GPA are considered in the admissions process. Your final-year GPA must meet the minimum requirement set out by the School of Graduate Studies (SGS). Your letter of intent and references are also relevant to the evaluation process. Meeting the minimum GPA does not guarantee admission.

lor_count.evidence_snippet: The deadlines for applicants to complete their applications, including two references, are below.
lor_count.review_note: Same page: academic referees preferred; managers or other engineering professionals may be appropriate referees for MEng applications.

eligibility_note.value: Requires the equivalent of a U of T four-year bachelor's in electrical or computer engineering or a related field (e.g. computer science, mathematics, physics), with at least a mid-B average in the final year. Final-year and overall GPA, the letter of intent and references are all considered.
eligibility_note.evidence_snippet: To be eligible for admission to the MASc or MEng program, an applicant must hold the equivalent of a University of Toronto four-year Bachelor’s degree in electrical or computer engineering, or a related field, with an average equivalent to at least a mid-B in the final year (as per the SGS International Credential Equivalencies tool).
eligibility_note.review_note: No numeric Pakistan equivalent on this page (it points to the SGS International Credential Equivalencies tool), so min_gpa_rule left out. Admission page FAQ: 'Both your final-year GPA and overall GPA are considered in the admissions process.'

language_waiver.value: Yes, possibly: for degrees from countries not on ECE's exempt list (Pakistan is not on it), an English-medium degree counts if the language of instruction and examination is officially verified, usually by a note on the transcript, or by an official statement your university sends directly to grad.admissions.ece@utoronto.ca.
language_waiver.evidence_snippet: If the degree was completed in a country not on the above list, the language of instruction and examination will require official verification. Official verification is usually provided in the form of a note on the transcript confirming the use of English as the language of instruction and examination.
language_waiver.review_note: This applies to applicants 'who will complete a degree where English is uniformly the language of instruction and examination'. If English was not used uniformly, a test is required.
